title: Kalman-based probe-signal smoothing and adaptive probe cadence to reduce autoscaler thrash
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: Rapid, noisy readiness/liveness probe fluctuations during traffic bursts are causing the regional autoscaler to oscillate (scale up/down) and trigger cascade failovers in multi-region setups, leading to transient SLO violations (P99 latency spikes and elevated error rates). Existing probe strategy (fixed cadence + simple rate thresholding) floods control plane and yields brittle readiness decisions when backend cold-starts or transient GC spikes occur.

Goal: Implement a probe-signal smoothing layer using a Kalman filter (or simplified extended variant) plus an adaptive probe cadence controller driven by traffic-volatility estimates and request-shape forecasts. Objective is to reduce autoscaler thrash by 40% measured as scaling churn events/minute during simulated bursts, and keep P99 latency and error-budget burn at or below current baselines during rollouts.

Scope: Prototype server-side signal smoother in readiness aggregator service, add adaptive probe cadence (per-region, per-pool) and corresponding autoscaler hysteresis tuning knobs. Provide canary rollout with experiment toggles, simulation harness, and dashboards.

Out of scope: Full ML-based request forecasting engine (we use lightweight heuristics + short-window statistics for v1).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canary region shows >=40% reduction in autoscaler thrash measured over 6 synthetic burst experiments; 2) No increase in steady-state request p99 > 5% relative to baseline; 3) No customer-facing 5xx regressions during canary; 4) Rollback path validated and automated; 5) Design doc, runbook and automated tests merged before release.
steps: Design: finalize Kalman filter state model and tuning defaults (process noise Q, measurement noise R) and fallbacks to EWMA if filter diverges
Implementation: add probe-smoother service module in readiness-aggregator (Golang); expose per-pool smoothing params and probe cadence controller in config store
Autoscaler integration: add input hooks to autoscaler to consume smoothed readiness confidence instead of raw probe counts; add hysteresis config (cooldown windows) for scaledown
Simulation: extend existing probe-sim harness (ENG-68211) with cold-starts, GC spikes, and multi-region failover scenarios; run guided P0 experiments
Canary: stage in single low-traffic region with circuit-breaker guard and progressive rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%)
Observability: create dashboards for smoothed-readiness, raw probe delta, autoscale decision latency, scale-churn rate, and error-budget burn
Rollout: automated progressive rollout with automated rollback triggers tied to SLO regressions and thrash thresholds
Documentation: update runbook and post-mortem checklist; add configuration guidance in console docs
risks: Filter tuning mistake could increase time-to-detect real failures and delay failover -> mitigated via EWMA fallback and conservative default Q/R
Unexpected covariance between probes and request shapes could bias the smoother -> add telemetry to surface bias and ability to disable per-pool
Increased complexity around autoscaler inputs may hide root causes -> keep raw signals available in dashboards and logs
Edge-case: long GC pauses may still look healthy if probes are delayed; require liveness hooks and synthetic warmup probes
rollout_plan: 1) Internal canary in staging with synthetic attack plan (3 days), 2) Canary region low-traffic (10%) 48h, 3) Expand to additional regions (50%) 72h, 4) Full roll over 7 days, monitoring for regressions. Rollback triggers: scale-churn > baseline*0.9 not improving after 2 hours, p99 increase >5%, or >0.5% absolute increase in 5xx. Automated rollback playbook in Ops runbook.
tests: Unit tests for Kalman smoothing edge cases; integration tests for autoscaler input pipeline; end-to-end probe-sim scenarios in CI (short run) and extended nightly load tests (long run). Load test IDs and artifacts referenced in links.
